title: What does it cost to read a human genome now?
subtitle: In 2001 reading one human genome cost $95 million. Guess today's price on a log line, then see how it outran even computer chips.
notes: OWID/NHGRI: $95.3 M (2001), $7.15 M (2007), $70,333 (2009), $525 (2022, latest), current dollars. Chip pace computed by me: $95.3 M halved every two years for 21 years ≈ $66,000 — and 2009 already reached it. Only this cast keeps the chip comparison. No log y on line_chart, so the figure stays a log number line with markers (2001, chip pace, 2007). An arrow between scale markers collided with their labels, so the 2007→2009 drop is a headline text instead. Scale tick size follows the page text block (36).
